case_study_insert.main_stem: Windward Sailing Holidays (WSH) is a private limited company in the tourism sector, running flotilla sailing holidays from Plymouth and employing a workforce of 36. Founded in 2011 by Elena Marlowe, it operates a hierarchical structure with autocratic leadership because safety decisions are centralised. WSH plans to invest $640,000 in two new catamarans, financed by a $400,000 bank loan and a $240,000 share issue that brings in new shareholders. It has fixed costs of $280,000 a year, a variable cost of $210 a unit and a selling price of $460, and produces 7,000 units a year in customer sailing weeks. WSH faces rising customer complaints about boat maintenance and a skills gap among new skippers, with safety a priority.
case_study_insert.appendix_1_marketing_ops: Operations Log — Summer 2025: WSH handled 1,850 sailing weeks with 14 reported maintenance incidents, up from 6 last season. Customer complaint letters rose from 11 to 29 per month, and 48% of a 250-person survey rated boat cleanliness as poor. Average booking lead time was 41 days. Six of 36 skippers lack advanced certification; external skipper training costs $950 per person while in-house mentoring is provided free by senior staff. Refund requests reached 4.2% of bookings.

appendix_2_financial_data.title: Extract from the Statement of Financial Position of Windward Sailing Holidays as at 31 March 2025 ($ '000)

case_study_insert.appendix_3_external_environment: Economic and Tourism Bulletin (November 2026): (1) The base interest rate has risen from 5.0% to 5.75%, raising costs on variable-rate marine loans. (2) The national minimum wage will increase by 6.2% from $12.40 to $13.17 per hour from April 2026. (3) Marine diesel and maintenance input costs have risen 11.3% year-on-year, while consumer spending on domestic tourism grew 5.1%.

questions.question_text: WSH plans to fund part of its $640,000 catamaran expansion with a bank loan. Explain two advantages for WSH of using the $240,000 share issue instead of the bank loan.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Equity from the $240,000 share issue requires no interest or capital repayments, so WSH's cash flow is protected while it already meets fixed costs of $280,000 a year. Money not paid to a lender can be used to fix the boat-maintenance problems behind the rising complaints and to train the six skippers lacking certification, protecting the $460 selling price and the 7,000 sailing weeks sold.

Point 2: Share capital does not have to be secured against the two new catamarans, so the $640,000 fleet investment is not at risk of repossession if demand for sailing weeks falls short. The new shareholders may also bring tourism contacts and expertise that help WSH fill the extra capacity. The trade-off is some loss of control for Elena Marlowe, but with a hierarchical structure and centralised safety decisions, operational control of the fleet can still be retained while the $400,000 loan stays smaller than it would otherwise be.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid advantage of a share issue over a bank loan (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation applied to WSH's $240,000 share issue, $640,000 fleet expansion and cash flow.

questions.question_text: WSH wants to fill the two new catamarans. Consider travel-trade brochure advertising, social media influencer marketing, or regional radio sponsorship. Which should WSH choose to promote the new fleet? Justify your recommendation.
questions.model_answer:
Travel-trade brochure advertising: Brochures placed with tour operators and travel agents can reach holidaymakers actively choosing a sailing destination, generating bookings for the 1,850 sailing weeks handled last season. They are expensive to design and print, however, and a 36-employee operator risks paying for listings that sit unused, with commission reducing the $460 price received. Brochures also appear slowly, which is a problem when booking lead time averages 41 days.

Social media influencer marketing: Travel influencers can show the new catamarans to exactly the domestic-tourism audience that grew 5.1%, with low up-front cost and measurable bookings. Content can respond quickly to the 48% of surveyed customers who rated boat cleanliness as poor by showing improved standards. The drawback is that results depend on influencer credibility and can take time to build, so they may not fill capacity immediately.

Regional radio sponsorship: Radio around Plymouth is cheap and reaches the local catchment that already supplies many customers, and it suits short-notice weather-dependent offers. Its reach is narrow, however, and cannot by itself sell all the extra weeks from two catamarans, so it is best used as a supporting tactic rather than the main driver.

Recommendation: WSH should choose social media influencer marketing, backed by limited regional radio for last-minute seats. Influencers reach the growing tourism market cost-effectively and can rebuild trust after 14 maintenance incidents; brochures are rejected as slow and costly for a business already funding a $400,000 loan, and radio is rejected as too narrow to fill a $640,000 fleet expansion.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: States simple promotional ideas with little reference to WSH.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Discusses advantages and disadvantages of at least two options in the context of WSH with some judgement.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Evaluates all three options in the context of WSH's capacity, complaints and finance with a justified recommendation that rejects the alternatives.

questions.question_text: WSH faces rising complaints about boat maintenance and a skills gap among new skippers. Explain two benefits for WSH of its autocratic leadership style in dealing with these problems.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Autocratic leadership lets Elena Marlowe make quick, firm decisions on maintenance, so the 14 reported incidents can be investigated and boats withdrawn from service immediately rather than waiting for group agreement. Given safety is centralised in a hierarchical structure, this protects passengers, reduces the 29 monthly complaints and helps defend the 4.2% refund rate, which directly affects revenue from 1,850 sailing weeks.

Point 2: Clear, top-down instructions also give new skippers unambiguous standards to follow, which helps close the skills gap while the $640,000 catamaran fleet is introduced. With six skippers lacking certification, decisive allocation of training and duties avoids confusion on safety-critical decisions, supporting the $460 selling price by protecting WSH's reputation and the contribution of $250 per sailing week.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid benefit of autocratic leadership (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual development linked to WSH's maintenance incidents, complaints, refunds and skills gap.

questions.question_text: WSH must close the skills gap among its skippers. Consider external skipper training at $950 per person or free in-house mentoring by senior staff. Which should WSH choose? Justify your decision.
questions.model_answer:
External skipper training: A $950 course per person gives structured, up-to-date instruction and a recognised certificate for the six skippers lacking advanced certification, which reassures customers after 14 maintenance incidents and 29 monthly complaints. It costs $5,700 in total for those six, affordable beside a $640,000 investment. The drawback is that skippers are away from boats during training, reducing capacity from 1,850 sailing weeks, and generic course content may not cover WSH's exact catamaran procedures.

In-house mentoring: Senior skippers can coach on the actual catamarans at no cash cost, keeping boats in service and teaching WSH's own safety routines, which fits the centralised safety decisions of a hierarchical structure. It is free, but it consumes senior staff time, can pass on bad habits, and gives no external certificate, which matters when 48% of surveyed customers already rate boat cleanliness as poor.

Decision: WSH should choose external training for the six uncertified skippers, supported by ongoing in-house mentoring. The $5,700 buy is small against a $640,000 fleet and buys formal certification that mentoring cannot, helping reduce the 4.2% refund requests. Pure mentoring is rejected because it lacks certification and loads senior staff, while training alone is rejected because it removes skippers from duty, so the two are combined.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Describes the two training methods with little reference to WSH.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses benefits and drawbacks of one or both methods in the context of WSH's costs and safety.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Evaluates both methods in the context of WSH with a justified decision covering certification, cost and disruption.

questions.question_text: Calculate and explain how WSH's management can use its cost, break-even and productivity data.

sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Break-even output = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution per unit. Substitution: $280,000 ÷ ($460 − $210) = $280,000 ÷ $250 = 1,120 units. Answer: break-even output is 1,120 sailing weeks a year.
Formula: Contribution per unit = Selling price − Variable cost per unit. Substitution: $460 − $210 = $250. Answer: contribution per unit is $250.

sub_parts.question_text: Explain four ways WSH's management can use this financial data.
sub_parts.model_answer:
1. Compare the 1,120-unit break-even output with 7,000 sailing weeks sold to confirm a large margin of safety of 5,880 weeks, supporting the $640,000 investment in two catamarans.
2. Use the $250 contribution to model discounts: a $40 price cut to $420 leaves $210 contribution and raises break-even to $280,000 ÷ $210 = 1,333 weeks, still far below 7,000, so off-peak promotions can fill the new boats.
3. Use fixed costs of $280,000 and $250 contribution to set the weekly sales target needed to service the $400,000 loan, checking the extra catamarans cover their costs.
4. Benchmark unit cost ($280,000 ÷ 7,000 + $210 = $250 a week) to monitor the 14 maintenance incidents and judge whether the $210 variable cost is rising with 11.3% marine diesel and maintenance inflation.

questions.model_answer: (i) Break-even output = 1,120 units | (ii) Contribution per unit = $250 | (iii) Four contextual uses: margin of safety of 5,880 against 7,000 weeks; discount modelling; loan-service target for the $400,000 loan; and unit-cost benchmarking at $250 to monitor maintenance and fuel costs.

working_marks: 1 mark for correct formula and 1 mark for accurate numerical answer in (i) and (ii); 1 mark per valid applied point in (iii).

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 2, evaluate WSH's financial position by calculating the current ratio and the acid test ratio for 2024 and 2025. Has WSH's financial position improved? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Calculations:
Current Ratio 2024 = 1.56 : 1
Current Ratio 2025 = 1.45 : 1
Acid Test Ratio 2024 = 1.25 : 1
Acid Test Ratio 2025 = 1.15 : 1

Detailed workings: 2024 current assets = $25,000 inventories + $60,000 trade receivables + $40,000 cash = $125,000; 2025 current assets = $30,000 + $85,000 + $30,000 = $145,000. 2024 short-term cover = $125,000 ÷ $80,000 = 1.56; 2025 = $145,000 ÷ $100,000 = 1.45. The inventory-excluding measure for 2024 = ($125,000 − $25,000) ÷ $80,000 = $100,000 ÷ $80,000 = 1.25; for 2025 = ($145,000 − $30,000) ÷ $100,000 = $115,000 ÷ $100,000 = 1.15.

Evaluation: Liquidity has weakened. Cover of short-term obligations fell from 1.56 to 1.45 because current liabilities grew from $80,000 to $100,000 faster than current assets, which rose only from $125,000 to $145,000. Cash fell from $40,000 to $30,000 while trade receivables climbed from $60,000 to $85,000, so more of the asset base is tied up in money owed by customers. The inventory-excluding measure fell from 1.25 to 1.15, confirming the deterioration is not just a stock effect. This matters while WSH plans a $640,000 fleet expansion and already carries a $400,000 loan.

Conclusion: WSH's financial position has not improved. Both the current ratio (1.56 to 1.45) and the acid test ratio (1.25 to 1.15) show weaker short-term solvency. The falling cash balance is the main concern, so WSH should tighten credit control on the rising receivables before committing further funds.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: States financial figures or changes without accurate ratio calculations.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Accurately calculates both ratios for 2024 and 2025 with contextual analysis of the trend.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Accurate calculations for both years with detailed evaluation of cash, receivables and liabilities and a justified conclusion on deterioration.

questions.question_text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for WSH of introducing a formal quality-control inspection of every boat before departure.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: Inspecting each catamaran before departure would catch the faults behind the 14 maintenance incidents and the 29 monthly complaints, reducing the 4.2% refund requests and protecting the $460 selling price. Reliable boats support the 1,850 sailing weeks sold and WSH's safety-first reputation, helping justify the $640,000 fleet expansion.

Disadvantage: A full inspection of every boat costs staff time and may delay departures, cutting the number of sailing weeks that can be sold from a workforce of 36. Checks can also give a false sense of security if they are only at the end of the process, whereas prevention through maintenance and training would address the six uncertified skippers more cheaply than the $950-per-person course; a rigid checklist may slow the centralised decision-making the business relies on.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage.
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual development linked to WSH's incidents, complaints, refunds and capacity.

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 3, evaluate how the base interest rate rise to 5.75%, the 6.2% minimum wage increase and the 11.3% rise in input costs will affect WSH. Which change will have the greatest impact? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Interest rate rise (5.0% to 5.75%): If WSH's $400,000 marine loan is variable-rate, the annual interest cost rises by 0.75% of $400,000 = $3,000 a year (0.0075 × $400,000). That is modest beside fixed costs of $280,000, and if the loan is fixed-rate there is no extra cost. Higher rates may also make customers cautious about holiday spending, but WSH can reduce this risk by fixing the rate.

Minimum wage increase (6.2%, to $13.17 per hour): With a workforce of 36, many deckhand and harbour roles are hourly paid, so the wage bill rises and cannot be avoided. The insert gives no hours worked or individual pay, so a defensible annual total cannot be invented. The honest test is against given productivity: 7,000 sailing weeks ÷ 36 staff = about 194 weeks per worker, so a wage rise is sustainable only if productivity holds or the new catamarans raise output; otherwise the $250 contribution per week shrinks.

Input cost inflation (11.3% in marine diesel and maintenance): The $210 variable cost is not broken down in the insert, so only a bound is honest: if the whole variable cost rose 11.3%, that adds 11.3% × $210 = $23.73 per week, or roughly $166,110 a year at 7,000 weeks (7,000 × $23.73). Even a partial rise would cut the $250 contribution sharply, and it applies to every sailing week sold, at a time when 14 maintenance incidents already signal boat problems.

Conclusion: The 11.3% rise in input costs will have the greatest impact. It compounds across all 7,000 weeks and directly attacks the $250 contribution needed to justify the $640,000 fleet. The interest rise is only about $3,000 and can be fixed, and the wage rise can be absorbed through productivity of about 194 weeks per worker, whereas diesel and maintenance inflation has no such immediate offset.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies external changes with limited application to WSH.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses the impact of at least two changes on WSH's costs, revenue or financing in context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed evaluation of all three changes in the context of WSH with a well-justified greatest-impact judgement and reasons for rejecting the other two.
